title: As-Samad, the Eternal Refuge
hook: the Eternal Refuge, whom all need (112:2)
tomorrow: asking God for the impossible: bold, or rude?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Ahad, the Unique, from the first line of al-Ikhlas. The line: unique. Today, the very next line, and a word that won't sit still in English.

Some words break translation apps. Type in the word some languages have for missing a place you've never been, and you get back a whole sentence. The second line of al-Ikhlas has a word like that. In Arabic it's short: Allahu as-Samad. Pickthall, translating it, needed a phrase: "Allah, the eternally Besought of all!" Other translators reached for other words: eternal, refuge, the one everyone depends on. So which one is right?
screen: `WORDS THAT BREAK TRANSLATION APPS.` → `ALLAHU AS-SAMAD.` → `ETERNAL? REFUGE? BESOUGHT?`

segments.voice: Maybe all of them. Commentators on the Qur'an have read As-Samad two ways, and English can only carry one picture at a time. In one reading, As-Samad is the one everyone turns to, the place you go when you need something. That's Pickthall's Besought of all: asked, by all. In the other, As-Samad is the one who needs nothing, who doesn't run low or wear out. That's where eternal comes from. Put the two together and the puzzle solves itself. Only someone who needs nothing can be the refuge of everything. A friend who needs you back is a good friend. A refuge for all can't be running low. The next line says it plainly: "He begetteth not nor was begotten." No one to lean on, no one to hand things off to. And here's the line worth telling a friend tonight. The Qur'an is just as plain about our side of it: "O mankind! Ye are the poor in your relation to Allah." Poor there means needy. Everyone. In this picture, needing isn't a failure or a weak moment. It's simply true of every person, and As-Samad is the address where all of it is meant to go.
screen: `TWO READINGS, ONE WORD.` · `THE ONE EVERYONE TURNS TO.` · `THE ONE WHO NEEDS NOTHING.` · `YE ARE THE POOR.` · then, large: `ALL NEED HIM.`

segments.voice: Write one line by hand: something you need this week that you can't make on your own, a yes, a calm night, someone's patience. Look at it for the sit without fixing it or apologizing for it. If you make du'a, the Name is right there: ya Samad.
screen: `ONE LINE: WHAT I NEED.` · `NO FIXING. NO SORRY.`

segments.voice: As-Samad. The Eternal Refuge: the one all creation turns to, who needs nothing back. Line two of al-Ikhlas.
For the road: all need him, says line two, and needing isn't failing. See you tomorrow.
